## NewsGuard ratings with the false-content criterion

Mirrors `scripts/inference/trustworthiness/6-create_newsguard_set.ipynb`, but keeps
the criterion that the notebook drops. The criterion was renamed in December 2023
("... false or egregiously misleading content"), so both names are matched.

```{r load newsguard}
ng_raw <- read_csv(file.path(src, "newsguard", "newsguard_twice_month.csv"),
                   guess_max = 100000,
                   show_col_types = FALSE)
names(ng_raw) <- str_trim(names(ng_raw))

crit_cols <- grep("Does not repeatedly publish false", names(ng_raw),
                  value = TRUE)
print(crit_cols)  # check: should be one or two columns
stopifnot(length(crit_cols) >= 1)

# check the coding of the criterion before recoding
ng_raw %>%
  select(all_of(crit_cols)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything()) %>%
  count(name, value)
```

```{r prepare newsguard}
recode_yes_no <- function(x) {
  x <- str_to_lower(str_trim(as.character(x)))
  case_when(
    x %in% c("yes", "y", "true", "1") ~ TRUE,
    x %in% c("no", "n", "false", "0") ~ FALSE,
    TRUE ~ NA
  )
}

ng <- ng_raw %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(crit_cols), as.character)) %>%
  mutate(false_content_raw = coalesce(!!!syms(crit_cols))) %>%
  transmute(
    Domain,
    Country,
    Score,
    # same month assignment as 6-create_newsguard_set.ipynb (file_date -> month)
    file_month = format(as.Date(substr(as.character(file_date), 1, 10)),
                        "%Y-%m"),
    passes_false_content = recode_yes_no(false_content_raw)
  ) %>%
  # same de-duplication as 6-create_newsguard_set.ipynb: one rating per domain and month
  arrange(Domain, file_month, Score) %>%
  distinct(Domain, file_month, .keep_all = TRUE)

# coverage of the criterion
ng %>%
  summarise(
    n_domain_months = n(),
    share_missing_criterion = mean(is.na(passes_false_content))
  )
```

As in `scripts/inference/trustworthiness/8-match_rating.py`, ratings from 2021 onwards are matched by domain and
month. Earlier tweets are matched by domain only, averaging across all months.
For the criterion, a domain counts as failing in that earlier period if it
failed in at least half of the rated months.

```{r ratings for matching}
stable <- ng %>% filter(file_month >= "2021-01")

ratings_month <- stable %>%
  select(Domain, file_month,
         ng_score = Score,
         passes_false_content)

ratings_domain <- stable %>%
  group_by(Domain) %>%
  summarise(
    ng_score = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    fail_rate = mean(!passes_false_content, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(passes_false_content = case_when(
    is.nan(fail_rate) ~ NA,
    fail_rate >= 0.5 ~ FALSE,
    TRUE ~ TRUE
  )) %>%
  select(-fail_rate)
```

## Match to untrustworthy links

```{r load links}
totals <- read_csv(file.path(src, "Austria-Panel-Untrustworthy-Totals.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)
totals

links <- read_csv(file.path(src, "Austria-Panel-Untrustworthy-Links.csv"),
                  col_types = cols(id = "c", author_id = "c"))

nrow(links)
links <- links %>% distinct(id, ng_domain, .keep_all = TRUE)
nrow(links)
links %>% count(year = substr(month, 1, 4))

first_month <- min(stable$file_month)

links_rated <- bind_rows(
  links %>%
    filter(month >= first_month) %>%
    left_join(ratings_month,
              by = c("ng_domain" = "Domain", "month" = "file_month")),
  links %>%
    filter(month < first_month) %>%
    left_join(ratings_domain, by = c("ng_domain" = "Domain"))
)

# matching check: share of links without a rating or criterion
links_rated %>%
  summarise(
    n_links = n(),
    share_no_rating = mean(is.na(ng_score)),
    share_no_criterion = mean(is.na(passes_false_content))
  )
```

## Results

Two definitions:

- **Link level:** tweet-domain pairs where the domain itself scores < 60.
  This is the cleanest measure.
- **Tweet level:** tweets counted as untrustworthy in the daily measure
  (tweet Score < 60; for multi-domain tweets, the mean score). A tweet counts
  as failing if at least one of its domains fails the criterion.

```{r share failing}
# (a) link level, untrustworthy domains only
link_level <- links_rated %>%
  filter(ng_score < 60, !is.na(passes_false_content)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_links = n(),
    share_failing = mean(!passes_false_content)
  )
link_level

# (b) tweet level, same definition as the daily measure
tweet_level <- links_rated %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    any_fail = any(passes_false_content == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE),
    all_missing = all(is.na(passes_false_content)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!all_missing) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tweets = n(),
    share_failing = mean(any_fail)
  )
tweet_level

# (c) distinct domains: share of untrustworthy domains failing
#     (a domain fails if it failed in at least half of its shares)
domain_level <- links_rated %>%
  filter(ng_score < 60, !is.na(passes_false_content)) %>%
  group_by(ng_domain) %>%
  summarise(fails = mean(!passes_false_content) >= 0.5,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(
    n_domains = n(),
    share_failing = mean(fails)
  )
domain_level
```

Robustness by year: the share of failing domains should not hinge on a single
period, e.g. the 2022 structural breaks.

```{r by year}
links_rated %>%
  filter(ng_score < 60, !is.na(passes_false_content)) %>%
  mutate(year = substr(month, 1, 4)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_links = n(),
    share_failing = mean(!passes_false_content),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Text for the Methods section and the response letter:

```{r report}
cat(sprintf(
  "%.1f%% of all links to untrustworthy sources (n = %s) pointed to domains failing the false-content criterion (%.1f%% of untrustworthy tweets; %.1f%% of %s distinct untrustworthy domains).",
  100 * link_level$share_failing,
  format(link_level$n_links, big.mark = ","),
  100 * tweet_level$share_failing,
  100 * domain_level$share_failing,
  domain_level$n_domains
))
```

## Sensitivity of the trustworthiness threshold

Reviewer 3 (comment 9) asks about the NewsGuard cutoff of 60. We compare the weekly share of
untrustworthy and trustworthy news across cutoffs of 40, 50, 60 (main
analysis) and 70. Untrustworthy = tweet-level Score below the cutoff
(mean score for tweets linking to several domains, as in the main measure).

Run `python scripts/analysis/1b-aggregate_thresholds.py <DATA_DIR>` first.

```{r thresholds data}
cutoffs <- c(40, 50, 60)

daily <- read_csv(file.path(src, "Austria-Panel-Daily-Thresholds.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(day = as.Date(day)) %>%
  arrange(day)

# trustworthy = rated and at or above the cutoff
for (k in cutoffs) {
  daily[[paste0("T_", k)]] <- daily$n_rated - daily[[paste0("N_", k)]]
}

# check: N_60 should match the main measure (count_max_caution + count_caution)
summary(daily$N_60 / daily$tweet_count * 100)

# weekly shares of all tweets (%), as in the main measure
weekly <- daily %>%
  mutate(week = floor_date(day, "week", week_start = 1)) %>%
  group_by(week) %>%
  summarise(across(c(tweet_count, starts_with("N_", ignore.case = FALSE), starts_with("T_", ignore.case = FALSE)),
                   sum, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  # drop incomplete first and last week
  slice(2:(n() - 1)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(starts_with("N_", ignore.case = FALSE), starts_with("T_", ignore.case = FALSE)),
               names_to = c("type", "cutoff"), names_sep = "_",
               values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(
    share = count / tweet_count * 100,
    type = recode(type, N = "Untrustworthy", T = "Trustworthy"),
    cutoff = factor(cutoff, levels = as.character(cutoffs))
  )
```

```{r thresholds plot, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4.5}
cutoff_labels <- c("40" = "< 40", "50" = "< 50",
                   "60" = "< 60 (main)")

threshold_plot <- function(t, main_colour) {
  ggplot(weekly %>% filter(type == t, !is.na(cutoff)),
       aes(x = week, y = share, colour = cutoff, linewidth = cutoff)) +
    geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("40" = "grey75", "50" = "grey55",
                 "60" = main_colour),
      labels = cutoff_labels, name = "Untrustworthy\nif score") +
    scale_linewidth_manual(
      values = c("40" = 0.4, "50" = 0.4, "60" = 0.9),
      labels = cutoff_labels, name = "Untrustworthy\nif score") +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%b %Y",
             expand = expansion(mult = 0.01))+ 
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste0(tolower(t), " news\n(% of tweets)")) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
          legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"),
          plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

p_n <- threshold_plot("Untrustworthy", "#7570b3") + labs(tag = "a")
p_t <- threshold_plot("Trustworthy", "#1b9e77") +
  labs(tag = "b", x = "Time (weeks)")

p_thresholds <- (p_n / p_t) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"))

p_thresholds

ggsave(file.path(dst, "figures", "ng_thresholds.pdf"),
       p_thresholds, width = 6.5, height = 4.5)
```

How similar are the daily untrustworthy series across cutoffs? High
correlations mean the temporal dynamics (the input to the VAR) barely
depend on the cutoff.

```{r thresholds correlation}
daily %>%
  transmute(across(starts_with("N_", ignore.case = FALSE), ~ .x / tweet_count)) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("N_", "N < ", .x)) %>%
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") %>%
  round(3)

# mean daily share (%) per cutoff, for the text
daily %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("N_", ignore.case = FALSE),
                   ~ mean(.x / tweet_count * 100, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  round(3)
```
